references.text: Here the actual action is described where Jesus makes clay (πῖλος) from spit and dirt, places it on the man's eyes, and sends him to Siloam to wash, which directly explains the words in verse 14.
These verses continue the account of the Sabbath violation, where the Pharisees discuss whether Jesus is from God precisely because he performed this Sabbath work (making clay and opening eyes).
Jesus defends himself earlier in the Gospel by stating that healing on the Sabbath is permitted, an argument that underlies the controversial action in chapter 9.
A previous Sabbath controversy where Jesus healed a man, and the Jews persecuted him because he did this on the Sabbath, creates a directly parallel motif to the event in chapter 9.
